thread:
deploy-bot: Started rollout of release v2026.03.19-rc3 to canary (5% traffic) in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 :rocket:

alice (deploy-eng): canary weight 5% across both regions. smoke checks scheduled: 2m latency, correctness, kv-stability.

synth-probe-bot: Ran synthetic scenario 'embed-small'. us-east-1 OK. eu-west-1: 95p latency = 210ms (baseline 60ms) ; error rate 0.4% (baseline 0.1%).

ben (sre): that's a big jump for eu-west. any infra changes in that region?

dave (eng-runtime): Not that I'm aware of. Kernel/driver rollouts were yesterday but that was in ap-south only. I'll pull metrics.

alice (deploy-eng): grabbing perf traces. can we diff kv-cache hit rates for the canary?

synth-probe-bot: kv-cache hit % (canary, eu-west-1): pre-rollout 88%, now 67%.

carla (release-manager): hmm if cache hit dropped that's probably routing/instance mix. Is it a model variant difference? We flipped to v2.3.7-quant-lite for canary.

dave (eng-runtime): Confirmed: canary instances in eu-west landed on machines with different NUMA config and the quant path behaves worse there. We'll see per-instance traces.

ben (sre): Options: full rollback, region pin to previous model variant, or continue (risk). Given correctness is fine, I'd prefer region pin to reduce blast radius.

alice (deploy-eng): Agreed. My proposal: pin routing in eu-west-1 to v2.3.6 (previous stable) while leaving us-east canary live. That gives us more signal and limits user impact.

carla (release-manager): +1. Also add a note to the release notes: "canary paused in eu-west due to latency regression; investigating quant path". We should open a ticket for root cause and schedule a postmortem if we end up reverting.

dave (eng-runtime): I can apply a routing override now: set route-model eu-west-1 -> v2.3.6 for 30m then re-evaluate. Command I'll run:```rb
sh opsctl route override --region eu-west-1 --model v2.3.6 --ttl 1800 --reason "canary latency regression"
```

alice (deploy-eng): please also trigger a longer synthetic run (10m) against eu-west pinned to v2.3.6 and compare tail latencies. synth-probe-bot, can you start that?

synth-probe-bot: Scheduling extended run 'embed-small-long' pinned->v2.3.6 in eu-west-1 for 10m. I'll post results in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ben (sre): I'll update oncall with the change window and keep watch on SLO alerting. If 95p doesn't return to baseline in 15m, we escalate to infra and driver teams.

carla (release-manager): Also add changelog entry to draft: "Canary rollout temporarily pinned in eu-west due to quantization perf variance on specific hardware." I'll mark it as customer-facing but non-blocking.

alice (deploy-eng): Quick sanity check command we used for smoke:```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY" -d '{"model":"v2.3.7-quant-lite","input":"short test"}' | jq '.latency_ms'
```

ben (sre): thanks. After override: I'll watch the SLO dashboards and set a temporary alert suppression for noisy metric spikes to avoid paging during investigation.

dave (eng-runtime): override applied. route change id: rc-20260319-0891. eu-west canary traffic now pinned to v2.3.6.

synth-probe-bot: Extended run complete. eu-west v2.3.6 95p = 62ms (back to baseline). us-east v2.3.7-quant-lite 95p = 205ms.

carla (release-manager): Good outcome. We'll hold the eu-west pin and halt increasing canary weight for now. Action items: dave - root cause investigation on quant path + NUMA behavior (ticket ENG-4122). alice - update rollout plan and schedule a gradual canary restart after fix. ben - keep SLO watch and update incident timeline if needed.

alice (deploy-eng): I'll update the rollout doc and set a follow-up sync in 1h. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary paused in eu-west (pinned to v2.3.6); us-east remains at 5% on v2.3.7-quant-lite.

carla (release-manager): I'll add the final note to the release notes and mark this as "monitoring" rather than rollback.

ben (sre): filing a short blameless blurb for the weekly postmortem board so we don't forget.

---

Notes: kept messages concise to reflect Slack style. Decision: pin in-region routing instead of full rollback to reduce customer impact while preserving signal from another region for debugging.
